title: unboringspec podcast script v1

Citation.description: A pointer to the exact line in the spec documents that supports a claim.

file.description: Document path exactly as shown in the '===== FILE: <path> =====' header.
file.title: File

line.description: 1-based line number as shown in the numbered document.
line.title: Line

Citation.title: Citation

name.description: A first name that sounds natural in the script language.
name.title: Name

role.description: 'guide' explains the spec with enthusiasm; 'skeptic' challenges decisions and gaps.
role.title: Role

Term.description: A word the voices must say in another language: a product name or team jargon.

text.description: The word or name exactly as written in the turns, e.g. 'Snowflake'.
text.title: Text

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the language it is pronounced in, e.g. 'en'.
lang.title: Lang

Term.title: Term

Turn.description: One spoken turn. Written for the ear: no Markdown, no lists, no file paths, no IDs like FR-006.

text.description: What the host says, 1 to 3 short sentences.
text.title: Text

sources.description: Optional citations for the claim in this turn (shown in the transcript).
sources.title: Sources

chapter.description: Only on the first turn of each part of the episode: 'hook', 'overview' (what it is), 'decisions' (the key decisions), 'to_decide' (what the listener must decide), 'close'.
chapter.title: Chapter

Turn.title: Turn

description: unboringspec podcast script: a two-host conversation about one spec.

language.description: BCP 47 language code of the script, e.g. 'es' or 'en'.
language.title: Language

tone.description: The tone the episode was written in: a preset id (e.g. 'roast') or 'custom'.
tone.title: Tone

hosts.description: Exactly two hosts: A (guide) and B (skeptic).
hosts.title: Hosts

turns.description: The conversation in order. Aim for 900 to 1200 words in total.
turns.title: Turns

terms.description: Words in the turns that are pronounced in another language than the script's: product names and technical jargon the team says in English. Natural voices say them in that language.
terms.title: Terms
